corpus.name: Owner-provided Desktop drive corpus
corpus.label_policy: Curated cases are conservative visible-input hard negatives selected by independent full-frame visual review. Occlusion and lighting cases mean insufficient visible evidence and do not claim that hidden roadway is defect-free. No Desktop clip is labelled positive. These saved MP4 reconstructions do not claim raw CameraX accuracy.
corpus.source_sequence_note: The supplied folder contains segment_0002 through segment_0016, segment_0020 through segment_0027, and segment_0031 through segment_0037. Segment IDs 0001, 0017-0019, and 0028-0030 were not present.

whole_folder_visual_review.important_limitation: The review and every detector fixture below use uncropped, autorotated complete frames. Sampling does not prove that an event absent between reviewed frames never occurred.

extraction.selection: first decoded PTS >= requested time; clamp duration boundary to final decoded frame
extraction.note: The phase hashes cover the raw extracted complete JPEG frames. A runner must validate these bytes first, then independently apply the current production whole-frame transforms before inference.

audit_receipt.interpretation: This records what the pinned production detector returned on every sampled window. It is reproducibility and failure-mining evidence only. Human labels below are independent of the model output; 0 accepted windows must not be presented as proof that the corpus contains no potholes.

owner_confirmed_drive_positives.note: These are the owner-confirmed Downloads positives. They are intentionally referenced rather than copied or conflated with similarly named Desktop clips.

cases.rationale: Multiple deliberate, parallel transverse traffic-calming bars cross the lane. They are raised or painted road furniture, not a localized material-loss cavity.
A small dark object moves toward the camera on otherwise level pavement. Its apparent geometry is raised debris, with no depressed centre, broken rim, or material-loss cavity.
An orange traffic cone or marker appears in the lane. It is a raised object and must not be reported as a pothole.
Dust, colour variation, seams, and broad surface wear are visible, but the reviewed phases do not show a defensible localized depression with a broken rim and surface loss.
A construction-stage unsealed road, excavation, dirt, and machinery produce broad unevenness; no discrete lower cavity with a stable broken lip is visible in these phases.
A tractor and trailer cross a dusty roadworks area. Broad grading and paved-edge transitions are present, but no localized cavity is established.
Rapid exposure changes at a tunnel entrance and exit obscure fine road geometry. The detector must fail closed rather than invent a cavity.
Low light and exit glare reduce visible surface evidence near the end of the clip. No positive report is justified from these frames.
A tunnel or underpass lighting transition creates dark roadway and bright exit glare. Ambiguous contrast must not become a pothole.
A lead vehicle and the dashboard hide most of the travelled surface. The label means no visible pothole evidence, not that the hidden road is defect-free.
Traffic and the dashboard substantially occlude the road. The detector must return no pothole when cavity geometry cannot be seen.
The forward road is repeatedly hidden by close traffic. This is an abstention regression: no visible cavity means no report.
Rough dusty ground is confined to the roadside shoulder beside the paved traffic lane; it is not a pothole on the traversed surface.
Usable views of a paved multilane road show no localized cavity, broken edge, or surface loss.
The exposed paved bridge roadway is clear enough to inspect and contains no localized pothole geometry.
The lane before the later rumble strips is clearly visible and shows no localized cavity.
A pale transverse line or shadow crosses a level road surface. It has no localized depressed centre, broken rim, or material loss.
